catalogue.name: Inventory.Reservation.Create
catalogue.description: Reserves supply for a source document line through Reservation Management.
catalogue.selectionDescription: Name the source line with sourceType, sourceSubtype, sourceNo and sourceLineNo (sales, purchase, transfer or assembly line).

subject.description: The source line is named in data (sourceType, sourceNo and sourceLineNo); subject is not read.

target.form: table no., subtype, document no. and line no.
target.description: The source line to reserve for: a Sales Line (sourceType 37), Purchase Line (39), Transfer Line (5741) or Assembly Line (901). sourceSubtype is the document type ordinal, or the transfer direction (0 outbound, 1 inbound), and defaults to 1 for sales, purchase and assembly lines and to 0 for a transfer line.

parameters.name: sourceType
parameters.description: Source table number: 37 Sales Line, 39 Purchase Line, 5741 Transfer Line, 901 Assembly Line.

parameters.name: sourceSubtype
parameters.description: Source subtype: the sales, purchase or assembly document type ordinal (1 = Order), or the transfer direction (0 outbound, 1 inbound). Defaults to 1 for sales, purchase and assembly and 0 for transfer lines.

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: Quantity to reserve, in the source line unit of measure. Greater than 0.

parameters.name: itemNo
parameters.description: Optional item number; must match the source line when sent.

parameters.name: locationCode
parameters.description: Optional location code; must match the source line location when sent.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Success when at least one reservation entry was created.

fields.name: entryNo
fields.description: First created reservation entry number. Pass it to Inventory.Reservation.Cancel.

fields.name: entryNos
fields.description: All created reservation entry numbers (one per reserved supply).

fields.name: itemNo
fields.description: Item number of the source line.

fields.name: locationCode
fields.description: Location code of the source line; blank when the line has none.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: Quantity reserved by this call, in the source line unit of measure.

fields.name: requestedQuantity
fields.description: The quantity that was asked for, as sent.

fields.name: fullAutoReservation
fields.description: True when the full requested quantity was reserved.

fields.name: sourceType
fields.description: The source table number, as sent.

fields.name: sourceSubtype
fields.description: The source subtype that was used, including the default.

fields.name: sourceNo
fields.description: The source document number, in upper case.

fields.name: sourceLineNo
fields.description: The source line number, as sent.

errors.when: Several source identifiers or values are missing or invalid.
errors.fix: Correct every errors[] entry before retrying; nothing is reserved.

errors.when: sourceType, sourceNo, sourceLineNo or quantity is missing.
errors.fix: Name the source table, document, line and the quantity to reserve.

errors.when: sourceType, sourceSubtype or sourceLineNo is not a whole number of 0 or more, quantity is not a number, or sourceNo, itemNo or locationCode is not text within 20, 20 and 10 characters (sourceNo must not be blank).
errors.fix: Send the integers as JSON numbers and the codes as JSON strings within their length.

errors.when: The source line does not exist.
errors.fix: Check sourceType, sourceSubtype, sourceNo and sourceLineNo.

errors.when: Unsupported sourceType or sourceSubtype, quantity not above 0, or itemNo/locationCode differ from the source line.
The source line is not an item line, or the Reservations domain is turned off for the company.
errors.fix: Reserve for an item line, or turn the domain on from the Inventory Setup page.

errors.when: No supply is available, so nothing was reserved.
errors.fix: Check inventory or incoming supply at the source location, then retry.

errors.when: The caller cannot change reservation entries.
errors.fix: Assign the Bifrost "Full Access" permission set (extended by Inventory write permissions) and a Business Central permission set that can change reservation entries.

errors.when: Business Central refuses the reservation while it runs; the answer carries its text.
errors.fix: Read the error text and correct the source line or the supply it names.

errors.when: The sales source item or line cannot be reserved: non-inventory item, Reserve Never, drop shipment, special order or missing shipment date.
errors.fix: Correct the source line reservation settings and retry.

errors.when: A transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. The error preserves Business Central's original text. Uncaught errors are Retryable only for types with effect write.
errors.fix: Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed.

effect.changes: Creates reservation entries that tie the source line to available supply, and commits them when the call finishes. Nothing is posted; the source documents and the ledger entries stay as they are.
preconditions: The Reservations domain is turned on in Inventory Setup.
The source line exists and is an item line that has supply to reserve from.

related.name: Inventory.Reservation.Cancel
related.useInsteadWhen: Cancel a reservation instead of creating one.

related.name: Inventory.Reservation.AutoReserve
related.useInsteadWhen: Reserve the whole outstanding quantity of a sales order line without naming a quantity; it reserves all or nothing.

related.name: Inventory.OrderTracking.Get
related.useInsteadWhen: Read which supply is tracked against the source line after reserving.

steps.purpose: Read the reservations that already exist before reserving.
Reserve supply for the source line and keep entryNo from the answer.
Read which supply is now tracked against the line.
Cancel a reservation by its entryNo when it is no longer wanted.

examples.title: Reserve 5 units for sales order line 10000. Replace the identifiers with your own.

chapters.overview: Reserves supply for one real source line with the same automatic reservation as the Auto Reserve action and returns the reservation entry numbers.
chapters.notes: Sales source lines use the same item/line eligibility as AutoReserve: inventory items only, neither item nor line Reserve set to Never, no drop shipment or special order, and a shipment date is required. Auto Reserve picks the supply, as the Auto Reserve action does, and reserves at most the requested quantity. A partial reservation still answers Success with fullAutoReservation false; when nothing is available the answer is PreconditionFailed and nothing is written. quantity is in the unit of measure of the source line. sourceNo, itemNo and locationCode are converted to upper case; itemNo and locationCode only check the source line. sourceSubtype defaults to 1 (Order) for sales, purchase and assembly lines and to 0 (outbound) for a transfer line. Bifrost commits the reservation when the call finishes; under Omit Commit the caller's transaction commits instead. Read reservations with Inventory.Reservation.Get and cancel an entry with Inventory.Reservation.Cancel.

result.conventions:
## Errors and warnings
An error response has `status` = `Error`, a stable `code`, the `error` text and, when they apply, `parameter` (the request parameter concerned, e.g. `lines[2].no`), `received` (the value received), `expected` (what was expected) and `nextStep` (what to do now). `hint` says where to read more.
When a request has several problems, all of them are listed in `errors[]` - each with the same fields - under a top-level `code` (`MultipleErrors`, or a shared code such as `InvalidLine` for the `lines` of a Create type) and a summary `error`. Fix them all before calling again. One problem is reported at the top level, with no `errors[]`.
Request values are checked first and every problem found is reported together. A Business Central validation error raised afterwards, while a record is being written, stops the call and is reported on its own: `code` = `BusinessCentralError`, Business Central's own `error` text, and `parameter` naming the request parameter being applied, e.g. `lines[1].accountNo`. Nothing is written.
Request values are read in one format, whatever the language: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; date-times ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset; amounts as JSON numbers (or a string such as `"1234.56"`, no thousands separator); integers as JSON integers; booleans `true` or `false`. Any other value is `InvalidParameterFormat` with `received` and `expected`; for an unambiguous local form such as `26.09.2026`, `nextStep` gives the value to resend. Every bad value of a request is reported together.
Answers are written in one format as well, whatever the language of the call: dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, date-times ISO 8601, numbers with a dot and no thousands separator, and the option and enum values of every answer except `Data.Records.Get` and `Data.Records.Set` as their English names, so a value read from an answer can be sent back. Those two answer the caption of the language of the call, for a person to read. The language of the call (`lcid`) changes captions and message texts, not these forms. Two things are outside Bifrost's control: Business Central writes its own texts (a ledger entry description such as `Direct Cost V00010 on 10/02/26`, the text of a `BusinessCentralError`) with the regional settings of the server session, which `lcid` does not change, so a date in such a text can be in month-day order; and a table view is read with those settings too, so write dates in a view as `YYYY-MM-DD` and decimals with a dot.
Both success and error responses can carry `warnings[]`, each with `code`, `message` and, when they apply, `parameter` and `nextStep`.
`UnknownParameter` refuses undeclared data keys before execution for every type whose effect is not read, including a missing effect. The root envelope option `strict:false` cannot opt out. Read types keep warnings without changing status, validationResult or domain warningCount unless the caller sets `strict:true` (next to type and subject, never inside data). Refusals list the keys and localized nextStep corrections; no business changes or successful execution charges occur. Example: {"type":"Memory.User.Set","strict":true,"data":{"memory":"test","memry":"typo"}} is refused.
`FieldChangedByBC` is a warning from Data.Records.Set: another field validation or the write changed a sent field after its own validation. `parameter` names data[n].fields.{jsonName}, counting from 0. Status stays Success. Compare the returned values with what you sent; follow `nextStep` to use validation order or send the field again in a separate call. Normalisation of the field itself, LCY, Dimension Set ID, BLOB, Media, MediaSet and skipped fields are excluded.
When a Business Central operation fails, the error can identify the request parameter being applied, the expected input and what to do next. That guidance accompanies the original `BusinessCentralError` after rollback, including a failed queued task. It does not change which writes are rolled back or committed. Guidance is cleared between messages; a message without it keeps its existing response shape. Recognized lock errors follow the `Retryable` rules below.
Some message types accept calls only through a particular path: a scheduled queue message, the Task API (`/tasks`), the in-product MCP tool server, another message type, or the Messages page Run Task action. Bifrost determines where the call came from; request values cannot override it. A call through an unsupported path is refused with `PreconditionFailed` and a `nextStep` naming the path to use.
`Retryable` means a transient lock or deadlock caught while writing or posting. `error` keeps Business Central's original text. `expected` is "no concurrent lock on the same records"; `nextStep` is "Retry the same call after a few seconds; nothing was changed." Bifrost does not retry automatically. Uncaught recognized lock errors are also `Retryable` for `write` types. Uncaught `read` and `irreversible` errors remain `BusinessCentralError`, because an irreversible operation may already have committed.
`ConfirmationRequired` is the preview refusal for an irreversible type called without `expectedCount`. Nothing was changed; inspect `expected` and the description before sending the same request with that count. `ConfirmationMismatch` means the count has changed or the sent count was wrong; nothing was changed. Inspect the new preview before confirming again. Feature apps use the same preview and confirmation protocol for irreversible operations.
Codes: `MissingParameter`, `InvalidParameterFormat`, `InvalidParameter`, `RecordNotFound`, `AmbiguousRecord`, `ConflictingIdentifiers`, `InvalidFilterField`, `InvalidLine`, `NothingToPreview`, `LinesSkipped`, `BlockedByWriteGuard`, `PreconditionFailed`, `PermissionDenied`, `LimitExceeded`, `BusinessCentralError`, `MultipleErrors`, `DeprecatedParameter`, `UnknownParameter`, `FieldChangedByBC`, `Retryable`, `EULA_REQUIRED`, `TRIAL_NOT_STARTED`, `ConfirmationRequired`, `ConfirmationMismatch`. The `error` text may be translated; the code never is.
